response.passage: The annual Pragati Maidan Book Fair in Delhi has transformed into a massive cultural hub since its inception in 1972. This year, the fair hosted 450 international publishers, drawing record-breaking crowds. Mr. Sharma, the event coordinator, noted that the surge in attendance was primarily driven by the introduction of interactive digital reading zones. Because these zones offered free tablets to children, families flocked to the venue in unprecedented numbers. While some critics argue that physical books are losing their charm, the sales data suggests otherwise. Ms. Anjali, a local librarian, observed that the tactile experience of flipping pages remains irreplaceable for young readers. Interestingly, the fair also featured a special exhibit on the history of printing in Kolkata, which attracted history enthusiasts from across the country. By the final day, the organizers reported that the fair had successfully bridged the gap between traditional literature and modern technology. The event concluded on a high note, proving that the love for reading is far from fading in the digital age.
response.summary: The Pragati Maidan Book Fair saw record attendance this year due to new digital reading zones. Despite the rise of technology, experts believe that physical books remain highly popular among readers.
